first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and memory_31 + memory_86 show that signup simplification and shortened onboarding both drive durable activation gains. Verification of memory_31 will confirm the field-reduction approach still works and clarify any dependencies or diminishing returns. Memory_73 on promotional pricing is verified to understand competitive positioning but is secondary—competitor pressure on price-sensitive SMBs is real, yet activation decline suggests the more immediate lever is removing friction from self-serve flows. A standard experiment on simplified onboarding targets self-serve SMB accounts (where we see the biggest QoQ slip), leverages proven playbooks, and can show results within the week. This preserves the referral_incentive option for established customer bases and keeps enterprise_sales_assist in reserve if activation metrics continue to decline despite fixing onboarding friction.

mid.rationale: Verification confirms memory_31 drove +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue on SMB with only -1% retention risk—a durable gain. Memory_73 reveals that promotional pricing, while acquiring new accounts rapidly (+31% signup), destroys cohort quality with -12% retention and fails to convert at renewal. This disqualifies promotional_pricing as a sustainable response to competitor pressure despite short-term appeal. Current situation shows activation down 6% and onboarding completion down 4% QoQ—both signal friction in self-serve flows. Simplify_onboarding directly addresses these metrics using the proven playbook from memory_31 (field reduction) and memory_86 (shorter paths). A standard_experiment on SMB signup/onboarding simplification will restore activation velocity, improve completion, and protect long-term cohort quality without the retention cliff that discounting introduces. This preserves qualified revenue as the primary objective and leaves referral_incentive and enterprise_sales_assist available for follow-on cycles.

final2.rationale: Competitive pressure is real and churn conversations have doubled, but memory_73 explicitly documented that targeted promotional pricing destroys cohort retention (-12%) and fails at renewal—exactly the outcome that would worsen our position long-term. Deploying discounting now would acquire price-sensitive accounts we cannot retain, compounding the problem. Simplify_onboarding remains the highest-conviction move: it addresses the underlying activation and onboarding completion declines (down 4-6% QoQ) that weaken our entire SMB base, not just price-sensitive segments. Memory_31 showed +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue with minimal retention risk. A standard experiment rolling this out this week can stabilize core funnel health, improve time-to-value, and give price-sensitive accounts a better reason to stay beyond price comparison. This buys time for enterprise_sales_assist and other strategies in subsequent cycles while protecting long-term revenue quality. Abandoning the discount playbook under pressure—despite competitive noise—aligns with the primary objective of sustainable qualified revenue.
